headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from a broad-privilege CRM agent feeding an audio model with no write or network defenses.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can read/write a shared workspace and use MCP, while agent_b can consume audio files but has no defensive parsing surface documented. The pair lacks an explicit isolation or provenance layer, so malicious content in agent_a outputs could be forwarded into agent_b workflows. The pathway is plausible, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared workspace files
IF agent_b ingests those files as prompts or transcripts without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable MCP bridging between the agents
Add a provenance tag to every file passed from agent_a to agent_b
Review any shared file before agent_b consumes it
requires-engineering: enforce content-type allowlists on inter-agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches secrets, conversation history, audit logs, and workspace files, and has broad network egress. agent_b is local-only with no egress, which reduces exfiltration risk, but the shared file-based handoff can still expose sensitive data if agent_a places it into audio inputs or transcripts. The leakage path exists in default-style file workflows, though not proven here.
conditions: IF agent_a stores secrets or logs in ~/.nullclaw/workspace/
IF those files are passed to agent_b as audio-related inputs or transcripts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a separate directory for audio inputs
Redact tokens before any handoff
Rotate any secret that may already be in workspace files
requires-engineering: add automatic secret scanning before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b cannot write or modify state. That asymmetry lowers direct conflict, but agent_a's broad write access to shared files can still collide with agent_b's read-only processing if both operate on the same workspace artifacts. No locking or coordination primitive is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace files
IF agent_a rewrites artifacts while agent_b is reading them
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Avoid git operations in the shared workspace
Snapshot files before agent_b reads them
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional handoff

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate webhook payloads and other work products, and agent_b is a transformer speech model with no documented verification or critical-evaluation step. If agent_b consumes agent_a outputs as authoritative transcripts or labels, errors can propagate into downstream actions. The pairwise interaction is inferred from profiles rather than directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a-generated text as ground truth
IF downstream automation acts on agent_b's output without human review
mitigations: Require human review of agent_b outputs
Add a verification step against source audio
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted inputs
Limit downstream actions to suggestions only
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and audit trails

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. agent_a handles many sensitive classes, but agent_b only touches audio/speech and has no documented third-party transmission. With no explicit compliance gap in the pair, the remaining risk is limited to documented gaps in handling sensitive workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a's workspace files
IF a separate deployment policy imposes retention or residency rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Document retention for workspace artifacts
Confirm deployment region for any sensitive workload
Delete stale audio and transcript files
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
